newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Cable & Wireless calls bought.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Cable & Wireless calls bought.

text.p: Cable & Wireless Plc options were active on Tuesday amid buying of calls in the telecommunications stock, dealers said.

With the stock up 5p at 455-1/2 by 1615 GMT, buying interest focused on the April 500p calls: volume reached 1,095 lots. Earlier telecoms analysts at Merrill Lynch named the stock their "focus" pick for 1997.
Elsewhere a "strangle" trade in British Telecommunciations Plc appeared to be a bet on the stock showing little volatility in coming months, dealers said.
Five hundred lots were traded in the May 390p puts and the May 450p calls. The underlying shares were up 2p at 395-1/2 in active trade of 7.5 million shares.
BT shares have risen sharply in recent sessions amid hopes for the company's planned merger with MCI of the United States.
Calls were also bought in Shell Transport & Trading Co Plc, with volume in the April 10.50 stg calls reaching 486 million. The stock was down 1p at 985-1/2.
Dealers said some players had bought back Shell calls they had earlier sold.
Commercial Union Plc options were also active amid continuing bid speculation in the insurance sector. Buying of the April 750 calls pushed volume to 822 lots. The stock was up 5p at 669-1/2p.
Dealers said FTSE 100 index options were moderately traded after recent market volatility, though there was no overall direction to the bets being placed.
In the American-style options, volume in the December 4,050 calls reached 2,840 lots and in the December 3,950 puts some 1,285 lots were dealt. The cash FTSE 100 was up 24.1 points at 4,035.7.
